holdings.companies.SOFTBANK.extendedHold: Licenses the processor architectures (ARM cores) that run almost every smartphone in the world and a growing share of servers and AI chips. SoftBank's principal asset and the foundation of the group's AI strategy.
Japan's third-largest mobile operator. The group's steady cash flow, now building enterprise AI services on top of OpenAI.
A personalised-oncology platform: it gathers patient genomic data and helps clinicians select therapies.
The French satellite operator. Since merging with OneWeb, a competitor to Starlink in low-Earth-orbit internet.
The SoftBank vehicle that houses the group's robotics investments. Boston Dynamics and other robotics companies sit inside it, valued together.
Japan's most popular mobile payments app (QR codes, P2P transfers). IPO'd in March 2026.
The merged Yahoo Japan + LINE — Japan's main internet portal and messenger, with e-commerce and financial services attached.
Japan's largest fashion marketplace — Zalando and ASOS in a single platform.
Builds Arm-architecture server processors for data centres. An alternative to Intel/AMD for cloud AI workloads.
The British designer of purpose-built AI processors (IPUs). A competitor to NVIDIA in training silicon.
The largest maker of CPUs and system semiconductors, now pivoting towards contract manufacturing of chips for other companies.
The third US mobile operator. SoftBank is exiting the position in stages — it sold the bulk in FY25, with the remainder held through forward contracts.

Autonomous robotic systems for large warehouses (Walmart, Albertsons). Amazon Robotics for everyone else in retail. SoftBank carries it on two balance sheets at once: $1.25B directly (Holdco) and $1.1B through SVF2.
China's largest e-commerce and cloud business. A historic SoftBank position, sold down almost entirely over recent years.
South Korea's largest e-commerce marketplace. Amazon's analogue: next-day delivery, its own logistics, video streaming.
China's main ride-hailing and delivery service. Uber's analogue, plus international operations in Latin America and Asia.
South-East Asia's super-app (Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand): ride-hailing, food delivery and finance in one place.
The Indonesian super-app (the Gojek and Tokopedia merger): ride-hailing, delivery, e-commerce and finance.
China's "Uber for freight" — a mobile app matching truck owners with shippers.
Smart glass for offices and buildings: it changes tint electronically, cutting the energy spent on cooling.
Europe's online used-car marketplace. The market leader in Germany, comparable to Carvana.
Norwegian warehouse robotics: a cube storage system with shuttle robots running across the top. Installed in thousands of warehouses worldwide.
The SVF's top 10 listed positions (Symbotic is folded into the Holdco group above). The combined listed portfolio is 45 current investments, $23.4B unrealised FV.
Through the Vision Funds — named private
The creator of ChatGPT and the GPT-4/GPT-5 models. SoftBank's principal AI asset — cumulative investment reaches $64.6B.
A British company building end-to-end AI models for self-driving cars. It teaches cars to drive through a neural network, without HD maps.
A screenless fitness band for athletes: it measures strain, recovery and sleep. The premium end of wearables.
A Korean travel platform: hotel booking, travel, and SaaS for hotels. The segment leader in Korea.
SBIA names these 13 individually in its "Late-Stage Portfolio Valued at $118B" table (87% of total private unrealised FV), but values them only in aggregate, not one by one.
Late-Stage Portfolio — valued at $118B in aggregate
The creator of TikTok and Douyin. One of the world's largest private tech holdings; building its own AI products at pace.
Enterprise backup and ransomware protection. Merged with Veritas; serves large enterprise.
A Mexican online used-car platform with inspection and warranty. The LatAm leader.
A Brazilian long-term rental platform with no agents and no guarantors. The segment leader in LatAm.
A corporate wellness benefit (formerly Gympass): one employer-paid subscription gives access to thousands of gyms and apps.
Licensed sports merchandise for every major US league (NFL, NBA, MLB). Also trading cards and sports betting.
An Asian booking platform for tours, tickets and local transport. Viator/GetYourGuide for Asia.
A British digital bank for mid-sized businesses. It underwrites SME loans with AI risk scoring.
An Indian budget hotel chain on a franchise model. It standardises independent hotels across Asia.
India's largest e-commerce marketplace (Walmart holds control). Amazon's competitor in India.
A British neobank: multi-currency accounts, cards, investments, crypto. A global consumer financial super-app.
E-commerce logistics for small and mid-sized businesses: storage, packing and order fulfilment from US and international warehouses.
Premium athletic wear out of California. A Lululemon competitor — sportswear with a lifestyle tilt.
Foundation models for robots: the "brain" that lets any robot learn a task and work in an unfamiliar environment. Series C at a >$14B valuation.
Robotic automation for e-commerce warehouses: systems that pick and pack goods themselves. Wholly owned by SoftBank since 2023.
A German company building collaborative robot arms for manufacturing. It turns classical industrial automation into something flexible and teachable.
SoftBank's own robotics subsidiary: creator of the Pepper and Nao service robots, now focused on the Whiz professional cleaners.
The world's best-known advanced robots — the Spot robot dog and the Atlas humanoid. Structurally inside Robo HD; SBG does not name it individually.
One of the world's four largest industrial robot makers (with FANUC, KUKA and Yaskawa). SoftBank is buying it from Switzerland's ABB for $5.4B.
An asset manager investing in data centres, telecom towers and fibre. SoftBank is acquiring it for $4B — the main engine of the AI infrastructure strategy.
A SoftBank + OpenAI + Oracle joint project to build $500B / 10 GW of AI data centres over four years. SB Energy supplies the power.
An AI search engine that answers directly instead of returning links. A competitor to Google and ChatGPT in search. SoftBank Corp. resells its Enterprise product in Japan.
SoftBank's own Japanese-language LLM company: the 460B-parameter Sarashina model. The goal is Japanese AI infrastructure independent of the US and China.
India's largest online eyewear retailer: its own manufacturing, eye tests and stores. IPO'd in November 2025.
Indian social-commerce: small businesses sell through WhatsApp and its own app. IPO'd in December 2025.
A B2B marketplace for Indian SMEs: wholesale trade in industrial raw materials (steel, cement) with embedded lending.
India's leading food delivery service (alongside Zomato). Also quick-commerce groceries through Instamart.
India's largest online store for children's goods: clothing, toys, food. A network of physical stores and its own brands.
SBG's Indian portfolio is 15 private investments, ~$4.1B unrealised FV.
A Colombian super-app: food, grocery and pharmacy delivery plus financial services. Latin America's most recognised tech brand.
A Brazilian fintech: loans secured on a home or car, refinancing, insurance. It targets the under-banked middle class.
Brazil's largest crypto exchange. Retail and institutional crypto trading across LatAm.
Small driverless delivery vehicles for the last mile (groceries, parcels). No room for a driver — cargo only.
The Swedish leader in buy-now-pay-later (BNPL). An alternative to credit cards for online purchases. IPO'd in 2025.
Source: SBG FY25 deck (13 May 2026) plus the SVF Q4 briefing (7 May 2026). Only names SBG itself discloses in official communications are included.

There are ~350+ private VF positions and dozens of listed ones that cannot be defensibly named — SBG does not publish a name attached to a number for them. Including them would require third-party aggregators (Crunchbase, PitchBook), which this list deliberately excludes.
